newsitem.title: USA: Arlington, Texas, looking at downtown project.
newsitem.headline: Arlington, Texas, looking at downtown project.

text.p: A $17 million project to revitalize the downtown area of the city is ready to move forward with engineering and design plans, the president of Arlington Chamber of Commerce said Thursday.
"The city council has asked us to pursue this further and we are extremely encouraged by this," said David Sampson.

The Chamber and other citizens representing Downtown Arlington Inc. have been trying for years to improve the landscape of the downtown area to attract new businesses and create jobs in keeping with the growth of the city of 300,000 people which lies between Dallas and Fort Worth.
But the city council has been reluctant to commit money for fear of being forced to raise property tax rates, which at $0.64 per $100 valuation is one of the lowest in Texas.

But after reworking the downtown project for two years, the downtown group appears to have come up with an acceptable financing formula. Sampson said of the $17 million, about $15 million would come from private investors, with the rest from the city.
Sampson said once the design plans are completed, they will be presented to the city council for further review before the project gets final approval.
